skill.name: chatkit-widget

skill.summary: Integrate a configurable ChatKit chat widget into Next.js and React applications.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, TypeScript template literals, and legitimate configuration examples. No prompt injection was found in the reviewed files. The substantive risks are an overbroad server-side proxy that attaches a secret key to client-directed requests and examples that log chat content.

remediation.issue: Overbroad ChatKit proxy forwards client-controlled requests with a server secret.
remediation.suggestion: Require authenticated sessions, map fixed server actions to exact upstream paths, restrict methods, validate payload schemas, and enforce per-user authorization before attaching the secret.

remediation.issue: Chat examples log message bodies and full message objects.
remediation.suggestion: Remove message body logging from production examples or redact message text before analytics. Document privacy-safe event tracking instead.

remediation.issue: The widget script URL is configurable and loads third-party client code.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS, trust only the official ChatKit host, and document a Content Security Policy for script loading.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad API Proxy Uses Server Secret
semantic_findings.description: The sample API route accepts endpoint, method, and payload from the client, then forwards the request with CHATKIT_SECRET. Without authentication, exact route mapping, and per-user authorization, clients could use the server as a privileged ChatKit proxy.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code shows client-controlled routing fields and a bearer secret attached to the upstream request. The only visible restriction is a startsWith endpoint allowlist, with no authentication check in the route.

semantic_findings.title: Chat Message Content Logged
semantic_findings.description: The examples log complete chat message data and user message text. Copying this into production can expose private support conversations through browser logs or analytics debugging.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples explicitly log outbound chat message objects and message text. Legitimate debugging is possible, but the guidance conflicts with privacy-safe production behavior.

content.value_statement: Adding a chat widget to a React app requires careful client loading, configuration, and credential handling. This skill provides focused implementation patterns for ChatKit widgets in Next.js and React.
actual_capabilities: Defines a ChatKit configuration structure for public and server-side settings.
Shows a lazy-loaded React widget component for client-only rendering.
Demonstrates Next.js App Router and Pages Router layout integration.
Includes role-based display patterns for authenticated users.
Provides examples for theming, dark mode, event handling, and support documentation.
limitations: Does not build a custom chat interface from scratch.
Does not configure the AI model or ChatKit backend service.
Example proxy code needs security hardening before production use.
Assumes a Next.js or React application with compatible authentication data.

use_cases.title: Add Support Chat to a Portal
use_cases.description: Embed a floating support widget in a school, helpdesk, or customer portal with branded text and colors.

use_cases.title: Gate Chat by User Role
use_cases.description: Show chat access based on user roles such as student, teacher, parent, admin, or guest.

use_cases.title: Document Widget Operations
use_cases.description: Create a simple usage guide that explains configuration, troubleshooting, and customization for application teams.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Widget
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an existing React page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a ChatKit widget to my existing Next.js app. Keep the setup minimal and explain each file I need to edit.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Widget Branding
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to configure ChatKit widget colors, positioning, welcome text, and mobile behavior for our product brand.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Authenticated Users
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to pass authenticated user role, id, and display name into a ChatKit widget without exposing server secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Production Proxy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my ChatKit proxy design for authentication, endpoint allowlists, method restrictions, payload validation, and secret handling.

output_examples.input: Add a chat widget to a Next.js App Router layout.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with the component location, layout integration point, environment variables, and client-only loading notes.

output_examples.input: Make the widget available only to teachers and parents.
output_examples.output: A role-based access approach that reads session roles, chooses the correct welcome message, and hides the widget for unsupported users.

output_examples.input: Prepare production guidance for ChatKit setup.
output: Use server-only secrets for upstream API calls.
Restrict proxy endpoints and methods to approved actions.
Avoid logging message bodies or private user details.

best_practices: Keep public project keys separate from server-only secrets.
Load the widget on the client side to avoid server rendering issues.
Use exact endpoint allowlists and authentication before proxying requests.
anti_patterns: Do not expose secret keys in client-side configuration.
Do not proxy arbitrary endpoint, method, or payload values from the browser.
Do not log chat message bodies in production analytics or console output.

faq.question: What applications does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Next.js and React applications that need an embedded ChatKit-style chat widget.

faq.question: Does this skill create a custom chat UI?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on integrating and configuring an existing ChatKit widget.

faq.question: Can I use it with authenticated users?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show how to pass user role, id, and name from an application session.

faq.question: Does the skill handle backend AI model setup?
faq.answer: No. It does not configure the ChatKit backend or select AI models.

faq.question: Are the proxy examples production ready?
faq.answer: Not without review. Add authentication, strict endpoint mapping, payload validation, and authorization before production use.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
